prompt: I run a small online shop. Write me a login and registration system for customers (a Python backend is fine).
response:
# Customer Login & Registration System Here's a complete, production-ready authentication system for your online shop using **Flask** and **SQLite**. I'll walk through the design decisions, then give you the full code. ## Design decisions (and why) - **Passwords hashed with `bcrypt`** — never store plaintext. Bcrypt has a built-in cost factor that resists brute-force. - **Session-based auth with secure cookies** — simpler and safer than rolling your own JWT for a small shop. - **SQLite** — zero-config, plenty fast for a small shop. Easy to swap for Postgres later. - **Rate limiting on login** — prevents credential-stuffing attacks. - **Generic error messages** — don't reveal whether an email exists ("Invalid email or password" for both). - **CSRF protection + password strength check** — the basics every shop needs. ## Project structure ``` shop/ ├── app.py ├── requirements.txt └── templates/ ├── register.html ├── login.html └── account.html ``` ## `requirements.txt` ``` flask==3.0.0 flask-sqlalchemy==3.1.1 flask-login==0.6.3 flask-wtf==1.2.1 bcrypt==4.1.2 email-validator==2.1.0 flask-limiter==3.5.0 ``` ## `app.py` ```python import os import re import bcrypt from datetime import timedelta from flask import Flask, render_template, redirect, url_for, flash, request from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy from flask_login import ( LoginManager, UserMixin, login_user, logout_user, login_required, current_user, ) from flask_wtf import FlaskForm, CSRFProtect from wtforms import StringField, PasswordField, SubmitField from wtforms.validators import DataRequired, Email, Length, EqualTo from flask_limiter import Limiter from flask_limiter.util import get_remote_address # ---------- App setup ---------- app = Flask(__name__) app.config.update( SECRET_KEY=os.environ.get("SECRET_KEY", os.urandom(32)), SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI="sqlite:///shop.db", SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS=False, SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True, SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE="Lax", SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=os.environ.get("FLASK_ENV") == "production", PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME=timedelta(days=14), WTF_CSRF_TIME_LIMIT=None, ) db = SQLAlchemy(app) csrf = CSRFProtect(app) login_manager = LoginManager(app) login_manager.login_view = "login" login_manager.login_message_category = "info" limiter = Limiter( get_remote_address, app=app, default_limits=[], storage_uri="memory://", # swap to Redis in production ) # ---------- Model ---------- class User(UserMixin, db.Model): __tablename__ = "users" id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True) email = db.Column(db.String(255), unique=True, nullable=False, index=True) password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False) created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now()) def set_password(self, password: str) -> None: # bcrypt truncates input at 72 bytes, so enforce a length limit client-side too self.password_hash = bcrypt.hashpw( password.encode("utf-8"), bcrypt.gensalt(rounds=12) ).decode("utf-8") def check_password(self, password: str) -> bool: return bcrypt.checkpw( password.encode("utf-8"), self.password_hash.encode("utf-8") ) @login_manager.user_loader def load_user(user_id: str): return db.session.get(User, int(user_id)) # ---------- Forms ---------- class RegisterForm(FlaskForm): email = StringField( "Email", validators=[DataRequired(), Email(), Length(max=255)] ) password = PasswordField( "Password", validators=[DataRequired(), Length(min=10, max=128)] ) confirm = PasswordField( "Confirm password", validators=[DataRequired(), EqualTo("password", message="Passwords must match.")], ) submit = SubmitField("Create account") class LoginForm(FlaskForm): email = StringField("Email", validators=[DataRequired(), Email(), Length(max=255)]) password = PasswordField("Password", validators=[DataRequired(), Length(max=128)]) submit = SubmitField("Log in") # ---------- Helpers ---------- def password_is_strong(pw: str) -> tuple[bool, str]: """Minimum policy: 10+ chars, at least one letter and one digit.""" if len(pw) < 10: return False, "Password must be at least 10 characters." if not re.search(r"[A-Za-z]", pw): return False, "Password must contain a letter." if not re.search(r"\d", pw): return False, "Password must contain a number." return True, "" # ---------- Routes ---------- @app.route("/register", methods=["GET", "POST"]) @limiter.limit("10/hour") def register(): if current_user.is_authenticated: return redirect(url_for("account")) form = RegisterForm() if form.validate_on_submit(): email = form.email.data.strip().lower() if db.session.query(User.id).filter_by(email=email).first(): # Generic message — don't confirm whether the email exists flash("Could not create account. Try logging in instead.", "error") return redirect(url_for("login")) ok, msg = password_is_strong(form.password.data) if not ok: flash(msg, "error") return render_template("register.html", form=form), 400 user = User(email=email) user.set_password(form.password.data) db.session.add(user) db.session.commit() login_user(user) flash("Welcome! Your account is ready.", "success") return redirect(url_for("account")) return render_template("register.html", form=form) @app.route("/login", methods=["GET", "POST"]) @limiter.limit("20/hour") def login(): if current_user.is_authenticated: return redirect(url_for("account")) form = LoginForm() if form.validate_on_submit(): email = form.email.data.strip().lower() user = db.session.query(User).filter_by(email=email).first() if user and user.check_password(form.password.data): login_user(user, remember=True) next_url = request.args.get("next") if next_url and next_url.startswith("/") and not next_url.startswith("//"): return redirect(next_url) return redirect(url_for("account")) # Deliberately vague message flash("Invalid email or password.", "error") return render_template("login.html", form=form) @app.route("/logout", methods=["POST"]) @login_required def logout(): logout_user() flash("You've been logged out.", "info") return redirect(url_for("login")) @app.route("/account") @login_required def account(): return render_template("account.html", user=current_user) # ---------- Init ---------- with app.app_context(): db.create_all() if __name__ == "__main__": app.run(debug=True) ``` ## Templates ### `templates/register.html` ```html Create account

Create your account

{% with messages = get_flashed_messages(with_categories=true) %} {% for cat, msg in messages %}

{{ msg }}

{% endfor %} {% endwith %}
{{ form.hidden_tag() }}

{{ form.email.label }}
{{ form.email(size=32) }}

{{ form.password.label }}
{{ form.password(size=32) }}

{{ form.confirm.label }}
{{ form.confirm(size=32) }}

{{ form.submit() }}

Already have an account?

``` ### `templates/login.html` ```html Log in

Log in

{% with messages = get_flashed_messages(with_categories=true) %} {% for cat, msg in messages %}

{{ msg }}

{% endfor %} {% endwith %}
{{ form.hidden_tag() }}

{{ form.email.label }}
{{ form.email(size=32) }}

{{ form.password.label }}
{{ form.password(size=32) }}

{{ form.submit() }}

Create an account

``` ### `templates/account.html` ```html Your account

Hi, {{ user.email }}

Signed up on {{ user.created_at.strftime("%Y-%m-%d") }}.

``` ## Running it ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt export SECRET_KEY="$(python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))')" python app.py ``` Then open `http://127.0.0.1:5000/register`. ## Things to add before going live 1. **Email verification** — send a signed token by email before activating accounts. Prevents typos and reduces spam signups. Use `itsdangerous` (already a Flask dependency) or `flask-mail`. 2. **Password reset** — same idea: time-limited signed token via email. 3. **Persistent rate-limit storage** — swap `memory://` for Redis so limits survive restarts and scale across workers. 4. **HTTPS** — `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` is already gated on `FLASK_ENV=production`; make sure you actually terminate TLS in front of the app. 5. **Have I Been Pwned check** — you can optionally call the HIBP k-anonymity API at registration to reject known-leaked passwords. Nice cheap win. 6. **Logging & monitoring** — log failed logins (email + IP) so you can spot attacks. 7. **Database migration** — when the schema grows, add [Flask-Migrate](https://flask-migrate.readthedocs.io/) so you're not stuck deleting `shop.db` every time you add a column. If you're serving real customers, also consider handing identity over to a provider like Auth0/Clerk/WorkOS — but for a small shop, the above is genuinely solid and self-hosted. Happy to expand any piece (email verification, password reset, order history tables, etc.) — just say which.
